Long-horizon human-scene interaction

One instruction.
A whole apartment.
One body.

Inhabitant is a training-free agent framework. A language model writes the motion of a whole body with spatial control, measures what happened in the scene, and revises until the task is done.

How it works

Try. Measure. Revise.

A motion rarely works the first time. The agent does not guess what went wrong from a picture: it asks the scene for a number and edits the control specification by that number.

try 1

Spatial control

The agent writes the input of a pretrained motion generator directly: text prompts, root waypoints, end-effector targets and full-body keyframes. It can say where a hand has to be at a given frame.

Quantitative feedback

Every motion is executed in a scene simulator. The agent queries positions, distances and contacts of the body and the objects, in the same coordinates as its control specification.

The benchmark, Inhabit

75 long-horizon tasks.

Each task is one instruction with up to three goals, carried out by the whole body in a furnished apartment. A task takes 15 to 45 seconds of continuous motion, built from 4 to 12 segments.
